The recruiter called. The interview is on Thursday.
Thursday? What are you going to say?
I am going to talk about the group project. And I am going to ask about the department, because nobody explained it.
Good. Are you going to send the resume again?
They already have it. But I am going to update the last section tonight.
I will help you with that, if you want. I did mine last week.
Really? Yes. Please. Are you going to apply to the same company?
Different one. They are going to hire six people, so the opportunity is bigger.
Six? Send me the link.
I’ll send it now. And Clara — you are going to be fine on Thursday.
I’m going to apply for an internship next semester.
I’m going to travel for a month in January.
I’d like to work in the marketing department.
If I get the offer, I’m going to accept it.
Can I ask you something about the position?

Okay so it is happening. The interview is tomorrow at ten, with the marketing department, and I am trying not to think about it. Tonight I am going to read everything about the company, and I am going to prepare three questions, because my cousin says the worst thing you can do is have no questions at the end. I am not going to memorise answers though. Last time I memorised everything and I forgot all of it in the first minute. What are you going to do about yours? Are you applying this month, or are you going to wait?

Good morning. Some dates for next semester, so please write them down. The internship season officially starts on the first of March. Before that, you need to do two things: register in the university system and upload your resume, both before the fifteenth of February. After that date the system closes and we cannot open it again. One more thing. If you are in your third semester, you can work twenty hours a week, and never during class hours. The companies know this, but some of them will ask anyway. Thank you.
